_readme: Performer-booking MVP eligibility, applied by scripts/fetch-events.js at
ingest. Every event in events.json gets an explicit `performer_requests`
boolean (default FALSE). Events flagged true show a secondary
'🎤 Interested in performing?' CTA on their card in the WordPress plugin,
which opens a short interest form emailed to the admin. See
PERFORMER_REQUESTS.md at the repo root for the full experiment doc.
An event is flagged performer_requests=true when `enabled` is true AND
ANY of these hold:
1. `include_open_mics` is true and the event has is_open_mic=true
(classification from config/open-mics.json).
2. It matches an enabled entry in `series_allowlist`: title_match is a
case-insensitive substring of the event title (hyphens normalized to
spaces), and venue_match (if present) a case-insensitive substring
of the venue name.
To turn the whole experiment off: set `enabled` to false (takes effect
on the next fetch run, ~twice daily, or run scripts/fetch-events.js).
To turn one show/series on or off: add/edit its series_allowlist entry
and set `enabled` on that entry.
Keep the cohort to local multi-comic lineups: open mics, recurring
showcases, independent productions. Never flag nationally touring
headliner shows (single named headliner at a major club) — a booking
request there is noise for everyone.
Deliberately a boolean for the MVP, not a status enum. If the experiment
graduates, migrate to performer_request_status:
disabled | testing | producer_unverified | producer_verified |
producer_accepting — the ingest stamping point in fetch-events.js is the
single place to change.

series_allowlist.note: Free booked bar showcases at Notsuoh, Social Beer Garden HTX, and Big Ben Tavern (~29 upcoming instances). Owner-confirmed booked shows (2026-07-24) — exactly the concierge target. No venue_match on purpose: all three rooms.
